src/manual/content/architecture

Architecture manual pages explaining ownership, execution flow, persistence, integration contracts and contributor workflows.

Parent folder

<!-- directory-inventory:start -->

Files and subfolders

Each entry links to the file or to the child folder's guide. Source summaries are navigation aids; they do not replace the implementation or its tests.

System ownership, startup and state

File or folder Responsibility
01-overview.md Architecture overview: smTO is a model-led agent runtime for durable tool execution and automation. The Controller accepts work and owns its execution history; models propose decisions; registered tools produce observations and effects. A browser displays that state and submits actions. A selected Gateway owns execution on its target computer.
07-state.md Conversation and run state: Accepted tasks and native checkpoints retain collaboration_mode independently of Agent Mode and Task Contract. Missing legacy values mean Default. Plan finalization stores canonical Markdown with its SHA-256 digest, source identity and timestamp. Clean answers and compact artifact metadata survive in trace/chat history.
16-source-map.md Source map: All paths are relative to the repository root.
24-gateway-platforms.md Gateway architecture and management: The controller reasons and authorizes; the selected Gateway executes against its host. gateway_core owns shared execution, file/HTTP contracts, jobs, terminals, TLS and controller authentication. Linux (gateway_agent), macOS (gateway_macos) and Windows (gateway_windows) supply platform configuration and supported lifecycle scripts.
45-server-lifecycle.md Server startup, login and durable shutdown: The Server makes its login and lifecycle pages available before controller restoration finishes. A single bootstrap owner constructs the controller, enters its lifespan, publishes readiness and later waits for durable shutdown.
46-gateway-state.md Gateway state, checkpoints and recovery: Each Gateway owns its execution state independently of the Server. A GatewayRuntimeStateHub holds live jobs, transfers, Docker operation reservations, replay nonces, workers and policies in RAM. Requests and worker events use that owner; they do not query jobs.db for missing or newer records.
57-system-flows.md System data-flow maps and navigation across request execution, retained state, every bundled capability family and supporting packages. Links detailed admission, reply, reconnect, storage and Gateway sequences to their implementation owners.
61-gateway-transport-flows.md Explains Gateway availability admission, TLS and controller pairing, signed HTTP requests, outbound mutual proof, correlated results and uncertain disconnect recovery through seven source-linked Mermaid diagrams.

Requests, execution, scheduling and results

File or folder Responsibility
02-request-lifecycle.md Agent and request lifecycle: Start with the system flow map for the surrounding packages. The diagrams here describe the HTTP request boundary implemented by RequestRoutes.
05-execution.md Execution and receipts: ExecutionEngine.execute_invocation validates the registered argument schema, resolves exact bindings, checks deterministic safety and ExecutionAuthorization, and invokes the tool's executor. Shell commands and Python actions use the Gateway; Python data transforms use a local worker.
06-result-chaining.md Exact results and JSON Pointer: Use one RFC 6901 string JSON Pointer for exact nested addressing. resolve_pointer powers bindings, read_result and completion checks.
08-tasks.md Tasks and recipes: A durable task persists a goal, status, attempts and checkpoints across API requests. route_groups/task_service.py owns task lifecycle and current-run projection. route_groups/tasks.py exposes task routes. Task execution re-enters the normal model-led runtime.
09-jobs.md Jobs, waits and resume: A job is an action that takes time, such as a long command running in the background. SMTO keeps a record of the job so the assistant can follow it later. You do not need to keep the browser open, but the computer running the work and SMTO's main service must stay available for progress to continue.
10-events.md Scheduled definitions, event/monitor dispatch and occurrence recovery. Browser sections trace Manager inventory and deletion, shared form encoding, prompt matching and explicit saves; diagrams separate local presentation, server timing/identity and later task execution.
19-scheduling.md Scheduling and concurrency: An activity is one admitted piece of work in a run. A batch groups proposed activities; a dependency graph determines readiness; resource admission decides whether ready work may overlap on the selected target. These layers remain distinct from durable background jobs and from the model's task board.
20-task-contract.md Task Contract Compiler: The compiler is an optional request-understanding step inside the existing run owner. task_contract_compilation_enabled defaults to false when no setting is supplied. The mode is bound to run state so a resumed run keeps its accepted interpretation mode.
25-artifacts-output.md Artifacts and output publication: agent_runtime/artifacts is production implementation, despite sharing a name with the repository's generated top-level output directory. The artifact store owns generated file identity, immutable versions, provenance and lifecycle. Collection registers actual files; previews, exports, download access and retention are separate responsibilities.
27-completion-normalization.md Completion and normalization boundaries: The model proposes completion. native/completion.py verifies the request's required evidence and checks; output/final-response contracts determine what must be delivered. A successful tool result alone is not permission to stop when other obligations remain.
28-execution-cache.md Explain verified read-procedure reuse and link its detailed proof/storage owners. Document prompt pins, Settings filters/removal, delayed eligibility, cross-tab invalidation and freshness limits with two browser-flow diagrams; distinguish retained regression intentions from current fixture failures.
59-activity-dependencies.md Explains graph validation, independent branch execution, human checkpoints, existing-receipt bindings and restart/Stop behavior through five diagrams linked to the source owners.
60-monitor-flows.md Explains monitor worker ownership, sample and stream execution, deterministic/model condition evaluation, trigger-task publication and cooperative recovery through five Mermaid diagrams linked to the implementation. Complements the monitor user guide without changing runtime behavior.

Tool interfaces, authority and information boundaries

File or folder Responsibility
03-tool-contract.md Tool and Skill contracts: src/agent_runtime/tools.py defines the only tool contract. A ToolDefinition contains:
04-discovery.md Tool discovery: native/catalog.py owns the CORE set and built-in control declarations. Core candidates include Shell/Python, Files, HTTP, Web, Artifacts, Agent Introspection, Task Scratchpad (KV), Memory put/get/search and schedule creation/inspection.
11-full-access.md Full Access and sudo: Plan collaboration applies a non-mutating operation gate before ordinary execution authorization. Full Access, capability grants and disabled optional checks cannot permit known writes or opaque/background execution while the accepted task remains in Plan. Allowed observations still pass normal authorization.
14-context.md Artifacts and context: Exact attachments and authorized resource-associated sources use scoped context IDs. Current read_context requests use a bound Context policy, Unicode character budgets and the returned continuation cursor. The deprecated limit argument still counts bytes within that policy; a missing policy does not select a legacy reader.
15-skill-authoring.md How to add a Skill: A new skill adds deterministic tools to the model's available actions. It must not add another semantic decision owner.
21-checks-authority.md Agent Checks and execution authority: Agent Checks are the named guard definitions in runtime_guard_policy.py. Categories include completion/evidence, mutation/execution, environment/target, routing, resource limits and recovery/convergence. Each definition records its enforcement owner, resume strategy and bypass meaning.
22-context-memory.md Context, compaction, Agent KV and Memory: The exact native journal is durable evidence. Model context is a bounded projection of that evidence plus current instructions, schemas, working context and user input. Context read policy constrains how stored material is accessed; it does not turn all stored data into automatic memory.
23-observability.md Activity, progress and execution visualization: The controller emits trace/activity events as the run progresses. The browser projects these into activity rows, tool detail, progress narration, timing and execution diagrams. A row is a view of server state; selecting it cannot confer scheduler or completion authority.
31-redaction.md Optional redaction and literal execution: agent_runtime/redaction.py owns optional credential classification and masking for runtime consumer projections. Optional redaction cannot authorize, reject, retry, repair, or change an operation. Canonical messages, arguments, HTTP profiles, files, receipts, working context, cache evidence and resume data retain literal values.
44-compact-guidance.md Compact guidance: Settings → Guidance → Compact guidance uses authored shorter equivalents of built-in model instructions. The master switch defaults off. Every independently supplied block has a switch, grouped by System, Task and runtime, Skills and tools, Recovery, and Helpers, then by its owning module. Settings search matches labels, identifiers, modules and groups.
58-model-decisions.md Native model-decision data flow and sequences for logical reservation, endpoint admission, complete-response validation, cancellation/deletion and bounded recovery. Separates inference capacity from task progression and external physical effects.

Target capabilities and integrations

File or folder Responsibility
17-gmail.md Gmail service boundary: The normal agent uses deterministic gmail.* capabilities in tools.py. The model chooses searches, drafts text and interprets results; the adapters perform concrete provider operations. Retrieved bodies, headers and attachment names remain untrusted external data.
18-http.md HTTP / REST Skill: For routine Proxmox server and guest operations, enable the optional Proxmox VE skill and use its domain tools. It reuses this Gateway HTTP authentication and transport implementation.
19-proxmox.md Proxmox VE skill and API: For setup and everyday requests, start with Using Proxmox VE. This page describes the implementation, session state and generated API contract.
36-desktop.md Desktop applications, processes and windows: Enable Desktop in Capabilities to inspect and control the selected Gateway's desktop. It starts disabled. Enabling it does not grant execution permission, change existing saved capability choices, or acquire OS permissions. Each invocation uses the run's captured Gateway selection and capability snapshot, including after resume.
37-clipboard.md Current clipboard: Enable Clipboard in Capabilities to explicitly inspect, read, replace or clear the current clipboard on the selected Gateway. It starts disabled. Enabling it performs no clipboard read, grants no execution permission and changes no existing saved capability selection.
38-screen.md Screen capture, OCR and context: Enable Screen in Capabilities to observe the selected Gateway's screen explicitly. It starts disabled. Enabling the skill, opening its UI, capability discovery and ordinary Agent turns never acquire pixels. Existing saved capability selections remain unchanged. Screen works independently of the Desktop skill.
39-browser.md Browser automation: Browser is an optional rendered-reading and interactive skill on the selected Gateway. The ordinary Agent uses deterministic browser tools; there is no browser Agent, locator model, DOM summarizer or screenshot classifier. Web remains the separate lightweight public search/read skill.
40-desktop-ui.md Desktop UI automation: The optional ui skill inspects and operates native accessibility controls on the selected Gateway. Enable Desktop UI in capability controls, then discover ui. Existing saved capability selections are preserved. ui.status reports availability independently of enablement; headless Gateways remain usable for other skills.
42-gpu.md GPU telemetry and configuration: Enable GPU in Capabilities to inspect and configure devices on the selected Gateway. The skill starts disabled. Discovery grants no execution or OS privilege. The Gateway advertises gpu_telemetry and gpu_configuration when nvidia-smi is installed; every operation checks current driver and device support.
43-web-research.md Web Research: Web Research researches public information while preserving the requested source, exact identifiers and filters. Enable it in Capabilities or accept its normal capability grant. It is optional and starts disabled; installing it does not widen saved policies.

User interfaces and documentation conventions

File or folder Responsibility
26-ui-surfaces.md Desktop and mobile UI ownership: Paths below are relative to src/agent_runtime/api/static/agent_ui/. HTML asset order and mobile import edges are the authority; source file size is not a reason to introduce a new loader or merge controllers.
29-source-documentation.md Source and documentation architecture: Current behavior is defined by source, then exercising tests and configuration schemas. Current canonical guidance explains it; file/symbol contracts document ownership nearby; generated references enumerate the current structure. Historical reports remain evidence of the version and measurements they recorded.
30-branding-compatibility.md Branding and compatibility: The public product identity is smTO, Small Model Task Orchestration. branding.json provides presentation metadata. BrandingLoader considers an explicit loader path, SMTO_BRANDING_PATH, legacy JARVMKS_BRANDING_PATH, application configuration and the packaged fallback. It retains the last-known-good identity when a selected replacement is invalid.
41-command-palette.md Command palette and desktop invocation: Press Ctrl+K on Windows/Linux or Cmd+K on macOS in the desktop Agent UI. The More menu also contains Command palette. The dialog contains the existing composer, attachments and controls, so a draft follows you between the two views. Escape dismisses the palette and restores focus. Dismissal does not stop a task.

Other files and folders

File or folder Responsibility
47-followup-queues.md Follow-up queues and continuation attempts: A queued continuation is an instruction for the next successful boundary of one task lineage. Acceptance stores the instruction and its selected resources. The controller reads the preceding attempt's retained context when it dispatches the instruction, so work completed after enqueue remains available to the child.
47-user-skills.md Writing and registering user Python skills: A user skill is an independently authored Python component exposing one or more typed tools. SMTO imports it in a separate process, discovers its contracts, and adapts those tools into normal agent discovery, capability selection, permissions, execution receipts and job controls. It does not require a controller source edit.
48-prepared-requests.md Prepared requests and queue admission: Preparing a request captures the settings and parameter references accepted for that request. Submitting it later must use that captured identity. A repeated HTTP request must not change the accepted configuration or start the same queue item twice.
49-conversation-lifecycle.md Conversation navigation and deletion: The controller reads conversation state from its runtime hub. Deletion first records durable intent and hides the selected conversations from normal access; an idle collector then retires their owned state. An HTTP success acknowledges that request. It does not mean every payload or recovery copy has been removed, or that an external operation has stopped.
50-conversation-task-coordinator.md Conversation task admission and coordination: The server accepts a conversation task once, stores its execution intent and advances it without requiring an open browser. The conversation coordinator connects composer input, task-lane ownership, native execution and UI projections.
51-gateway-local-ai.md Gateway Local AI runtimes: Local AI Runtimes is an optional skill for inspecting and managing model servers on the selected Gateway. It starts disabled. Enable it through the ordinary capability controls; existing permissions, confirmations and target selection still apply. Its operations inspect metadata and manage processes/model storage without making helper inference calls.
52-native-files.md Native Files and mutation receipts: The Files skill operates on the selected Gateway's filesystem. It offers bounded reads, discovery, metadata and content hashes, text comparisons, exact edits and file management. File contents and paths are data; the adapter does not convert a File call into a shell command. Existing Shell commands remain separate tools.
53-command-working-context.md Command setup and Working Context: Supported Shell commands can leave verified setup facts for later work in the same conversation: a repository root, an SSH endpoint and host key, a Kubernetes context and namespace, or a SLURM cluster configuration. These records reduce repeated setup discovery.
54-recipes-workflows.md Workflow definitions, invocation and recovery: The current Workflow interface stores a reviewed request and starts a fresh ordinary Agent task for each invocation. Its HTTP routes accept saved_request_v1.
55-parameter-storage-bindings.md Parameter storage, acceptance and exact inputs: Parameters and Database explains operator setup. This guide separates live saved records, accepted task inputs and consumer projections. Editing a saved ordinary parameter changes future acceptance; it does not replace the literal value already owned by a queued or running task.
56-notifications.md Notification publication and observation: separates canonical event-store records, public projection, update-stream invalidations, browser delivery and explicit inbox mutations. Diagrams trace silent hydration, cross-tab deduplication, native/toast selection, deep links and read-only upcoming reminders.
62-inference-lifecycle.md Explains optional Controller inference ownership through eight diagrams: management inputs, native receipt-gated intents, endpoint admission, instance transitions, rollback, startup recovery, subsystem lifecycle and versioned model binding/dispatch. Links each boundary to its implementation and isolated fixtures.
63-inference-observation.md Managed inference observation: separates active request occupancy, selected model status, explicit lifecycle commands, browser freshness/polling, capture leases, worker telemetry, timeline sampling and export. Diagrams include status invalidation, generation fences and page suspension without server cancellation.
64-portal-launch.md Traces shared Portal planning, requested/resolved snapshots, distributed generation launch, resource admission, readiness, retry, worker cleanup and restart intent. Eight data-flow and sequence diagrams connect source owners with isolated control-flow evidence.
65-gateway-state-flows.md Trace Gateway RAM transactions, exclusive ownership, checkpoint publication, independent safety evidence, nonce consumption, worker-exit reconciliation and bounded shutdown with data-flow and sequence diagrams.
66-composer-resource-flows.md Trace composer namespace loading, metadata search, cache and stale-response checks, resource selection, attachment grants and editor cleanup through six data-flow and sequence diagrams.
67-instruction-editor-flows.md Trace editor-local resource drafts, exact retry identity, saved steering application, cancellation uncertainty and accepted continuation children through six diagrams linked to their source owners.
68-prompt-recall-flows.md Trace bounded prompt history, atomic usage updates, Unicode similarity groups, background cache/cancellation and per-input text completion through five data-flow and sequence diagrams.
69-browser-queue-flows.md Follow browser task submission, uncertain retry identity, canonical lane reads, explicit queue actions, dependency restoration and continuation-panel deletion through six data-flow and sequence diagrams.
70-mobile-queue-flows.md Trace mobile intent capture, exact-body retry identities, dependency restoration, canonical queue reads and sheet mutation/close boundaries through three data-flow and sequence diagrams.
71-native-control-flows.md Trace native UI observation, explicit lifecycle commands, attempt/queue identity, attachment fences, foreground decisions and accepted-reply handoff through seven data-flow and sequence diagrams.
72-execution-timeline-flows.md Execution snapshot and timeline flows: traces read-only native/trace/task joins, interval and wait reconstruction, overlap analysis, bounded text summaries and event-driven disclosure caching. Explains live-clock limits, retry, copy and teardown with four diagrams.
73-memory-editor-flows.md Memory Editor reads, revisions and persistence: traces inventory paging and generation fences, unsaved form state, explicit revision-checked mutations, preserved project bindings and separate checkpoint confirmation with four diagrams.
74-workflow-browser-flows.md Workflow browser, editor and submission flows: traces draft/candidate previews, revision-checked saves, element-local run retries, library refreshes, history/delete and pinned schedule binding with five data-flow and sequence diagrams.
75-backup-browser-flows.md Backup export, staged import and recovery flows: diagrams separate Settings save, server jobs, browser download handoff, cancellation races, preview tokens, pending import and offline generation commit/recovery. Links temporary recovery retention and legacy journal behavior to their source owners.
